## Comparison

Both traces solve the same 3-coloring problem with nearly identical strategies: identify B as the highest-degree node, force its neighbors into the remaining two colors, deduce C/D/E from internal edges, then propagate to G, F, H, I, A. Both find valid solutions (Trace 1: G=Green; Trace 2: G=Red — both valid since all of G's neighbors end up Blue).

Both traces open an explicit alternative-solution branch after finding their first solution (Trace 1: "What if I chose C=Green?"; Trace 2: "Let's try to find another solution"). In each case the branch produces a second valid coloring whose existence is used to confirm the first solution suffices — a paying-off CYCLE in both.

The major divergence is in verification volume. Trace 1 re-executes edge checks and node-by-node checks at least 5–6 separate times at the end; Trace 2 does similarly but slightly fewer distinct rounds. Both exhibit heavy LOOP behavior, though Trace 1's is more extreme.

---

## Trace 1

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's check if there is any other possibility" end="The first solution I found seems robust" basis=Opens C=Green alternative after Solution 1 is found, explores it to a full second coloring, then uses the result to conclude Solution 1 is sufficient.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's verify the solution one last time with a fresh eye." end="All edges valid." basis=Re-executes the same 13-edge verification already completed after finding Solution 1, adding no new constraint.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's double check the adjacency list provided in the prompt again to ensure no typo." end="Everything seems consistent." basis=Re-lists and re-verifies all 13 edges against Solution 1 a third time, no new information added.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's verify the solution one more time." end="All OK." basis=Fourth full edge-by-edge re-verification of the same solution already checked multiple times.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, check C again." end="Everything is perfect." basis=Full node-by-node re-verification of every node's constraints, repeating checks already done in prior edge-verification blocks.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, check F again." end="Everything holds." basis=Second complete node-by-node re-verification, re-executing the identical per-node checks just completed above.

---

## Trace 2

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's try to find another solution just in case" end="So providing one valid assignment is sufficient." basis=Opens C=3 alternative after Solution 1 is found, explores it to a full second coloring, then uses the result to conclude one solution is enough.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let me re-read the adjacency list to ensure I didn't miss any edge." end="My check covered all." basis=Re-reads and re-checks the same 13-edge list already enumerated and verified moments earlier.

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, check C again." end="This works." basis=Full node-by-node re-verification of all 9 nodes' constraints, repeating edge checks already completed in prior verification blocks; the pattern then repeats again immediately after.
